input.strategy_title: Make RHOAI more usable for enterprise teams
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Several strategic accounts have told field teams that RHOAI "feels hard to use
at enterprise scale". Feedback arrived through different channels and has not
been consolidated; the quotes below are representative but partially
contradictory. Leadership wants visible usability progress this release.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | — | Administration should be simpler. One account wants fewer configuration options exposed ("too many knobs"), another explicitly wants more fine-grained controls per project. |
| HLR-2 | — | Onboarding a new data scientist should take "less than a day". It is not defined what onboarding includes or where the day is currently spent. |
| HLR-3 | — | The platform should "integrate better" with existing enterprise tooling. No specific tools were named in the consolidated feedback. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Publish a whitepaper describing enterprise usability best practices on RHOAI. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks

## Out of Scope

Nothing has been explicitly scoped out.

## Open Questions

1. Which accounts' feedback takes precedence when requirements conflict (HLR-1)?
2. What does "onboarding" cover for HLR-2 — cluster access, project setup,
   first workbench, or first deployed model?
3. Which enterprise tools does HLR-3 actually mean?

# Streamline the administration configuration surface

## Description

Conditional implementation plan, active only if the enterprise feedback investigation
selects the simplification direction for the administration requirement (the account
feedback calling for fewer exposed configuration options takes precedence). This epic
reduces the number of administration configuration options exposed to administrators in
the RHOAI Dashboard, replacing removed knobs with curated defaults, with the specific
option set defined by the investigation's decision record.

## Scope

- Reduce the set of administration configuration options exposed in the Dashboard
  administration surface, per the option list in the investigation decision record. The
  configuration surface is the Dashboard admin settings backed by the OdhDashboardConfig
  custom resource, as documented in the RHOAI architecture context.
- Provide curated defaults for every removed or hidden option that preserve current
  behavior for existing deployments.
- Make the changed configuration surface reversible via a feature flag or equivalent
  rollback mechanism, since this modifies an existing capability.
- Update captions, references, and settings documentation that fall out of the same
  change (no new content authored).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The count of exposed administration configuration options matches the reduced set
  defined in the investigation decision record.
- Deployments that used the previous defaults exhibit unchanged behavior after the
  change (defaults preserve prior outcomes).
- The changed surface is reversible via a feature flag or documented rollback path.
- Every removed option has a documented default value, and existing administrator
  workflows are regression-tested against the reduced surface.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (administration should be simpler): implements the simplification direction —
  fewer exposed configuration options with curated defaults.

# Add fine-grained per-project administration controls

## Description

Conditional implementation plan, active only if the enterprise feedback investigation
selects the fine-grained direction for the administration requirement (the account
feedback calling for more per-project controls takes precedence). This epic adds
per-project granularity to RHOAI administration controls in the Dashboard, with the
specific control set defined by the investigation's decision record.

## Scope

- Add per-project administration controls to the Dashboard administration surface, per
  the control list in the investigation decision record. The existing configuration
  surface (Dashboard admin settings backed by the OdhDashboardConfig custom resource, and
  the per-workbench override pattern used for culling settings) is the documented
  foundation; the specific mechanism is an implementation decision for the team.
- Preserve platform-wide defaults wherever no per-project override is set, so existing
  deployments are unaffected until an administrator opts in.
- Document the new control surface and the precedence order between platform-wide
  defaults and per-project overrides.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-project administration controls operate as defined in the investigation decision
  record, and a per-project override takes precedence over the platform-wide default for
  the affected project only.
- Projects without an override behave identically to the current platform-wide defaults.
- The precedence rules and available controls are documented.
- Existing platform-wide administration workflows are regression-tested and unaffected
  where no override exists.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (administration should be simpler): implements the fine-grained direction —
  more granular per-project administration controls.

# Implement layered administration defaults with opt-in advanced controls

## Description

Conditional implementation plan, active only if the enterprise feedback investigation
selects the layered resolution for the administration requirement (both accounts' needs
are met: a simple default experience plus opt-in fine-grained control). This epic
introduces curated defaults that hide advanced administration options behind an opt-in
surface in the RHOAI Dashboard, so administrators see fewer knobs by default while
retaining full per-project control when needed. The specific option and control sets are
defined by the investigation's decision record.

## Scope

- Implement a default administration view in the Dashboard that exposes only the curated
  set of options defined in the investigation decision record, backed by the OdhDashboardConfig
  configuration surface documented in the RHOAI architecture context.
- Implement an opt-in advanced surface exposing the fine-grained per-project controls
  defined in the decision record, available to administrators who need them.
- Make the layered presentation reversible via a feature flag or equivalent rollback
  mechanism, since this modifies an existing capability.
- Document the default view, the advanced surface, and the precedence between curated
  defaults, platform-wide settings, and per-project overrides.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The default administration view exposes exactly the curated option set from the
  decision record; the advanced controls are hidden until opted into.
- Opting in exposes the full fine-grained control set, and per-project overrides take
  precedence over curated defaults for the affected project only.
- Deployments that do not opt in behave as if only the curated defaults exist (no
  behavior change for existing default configurations).
- The layered presentation is reversible via a feature flag or documented rollback path.
- The default view, advanced surface, and precedence rules are documented.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (administration should be simpler): implements the layered resolution —
  curated defaults satisfying the "fewer knobs" account, with opt-in per-project controls
  satisfying the fine-grained account.

# Consolidate enterprise feedback and set the administration usability direction

## Description

This investigation resolves the two unknowns that block all configuration and
integration work in the strategy. The problem statement records that enterprise account
feedback "arrived through different channels and has not been consolidated" and is
"partially contradictory". This investigation consolidates that feedback into a single
record, decides a precedence policy for conflicting requirements, and produces a decision
record that (a) selects the direction for the administration requirement — simplifying
the exposed configuration surface, adding fine-grained per-project controls, or a layered
combination — and (b) names the concrete enterprise tools the integration requirement
refers to. The decision record is the input from which the follow-up implementation
decomposition is performed.

## Scope

- Consolidate all enterprise account feedback referenced by the strategy (field team
  reports, strategic account channels) into a single record in which every requirement is
  traceable to its source account(s) and channel.
- Define a precedence policy for conflicting feedback (which accounts' input carries more
  weight, and on what basis) and apply it to the HLR-1 conflict: one account wants fewer
  exposed configuration options, another wants more fine-grained per-project controls.
- Select exactly one HLR-1 direction: simplification, fine-grained per-project controls,
  or a layered resolution (curated defaults with opt-in advanced controls). Record the
  rationale and which conditional implementation plan the selection activates.
- Identify and name the specific enterprise tools behind the integration requirement
  (HLR-3), with per-tool rationale drawn from the consolidated feedback; if the feedback
  contains no tool names, record that finding explicitly and recommend an escalation path
  (e.g. a structured account survey).
- Annotate every decision with the downstream work it enables or gates, so a follow-up
  decomposition can be performed directly from the decision record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A consolidated feedback record exists that merges every feedback channel referenced by
  the strategy, with each requirement traceable to its source account(s).
- The decision record states an explicit precedence policy and applies it to the HLR-1
  conflict, selecting exactly one of: simplification, fine-grained per-project controls,
  or layered resolution.
- The decision record names the concrete enterprise tools for the integration
  requirement, or documents that no tools could be identified and defines the escalation
  path.
- The decision record is reviewed and accepted by product management.
- Every decision is annotated with the downstream work it gates.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (administration should be simpler): resolves the contradictory requirement
  and selects the implementation direction.
- **HLR-3** (integrate better with existing enterprise tooling): identifies the concrete
  tool targets the requirement refers to.

# Define data scientist onboarding scope and establish the current-state baseline

## Description

This investigation resolves the unknown blocking the onboarding requirement (HLR-2):
"onboarding a new data scientist should take less than a day" is stated without defining
what onboarding includes or where the day is currently spent. The investigation produces
(a) a ratified definition of what onboarding covers, (b) a current-state analysis of the
onboarding journey, and (c) a baseline (or a measurement plan) for where time is spent
today, so the one-day target becomes measurable and the improvement work can be
decomposed.

## Scope

- Propose, and obtain product ratification of, a definition of "data scientist
  onboarding" that states which facets it covers — the strategy enumerates the candidates:
  cluster access, project setup, first workbench, first deployed model.
- Produce a current-state analysis of each covered facet's path as it exists today
  (project creation in the console, workbench spawning and image selection, model serving
  enablement), with each step cited to public documentation or component source.
- Establish where onboarding time is currently spent: extract a baseline from existing
  telemetry or usage data where available, and where no data exists, define the
  measurement method (instrumentation or structured user research) that will produce it.
- Compare the current state against the "less than a day" target and identify the largest
  quantified friction points.
- Recommend which friction points to address, as the input for the follow-up
  implementation decomposition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written onboarding definition exists, approved by product management, that
  enumerates exactly which facets (cluster access, project setup, first workbench, first
  deployed model) onboarding covers.
- The current-state onboarding path is documented step by step, with each step cited to
  documentation or component source.
- A time baseline for the defined onboarding path exists, or — where no data is
  available — a defined measurement method with the data source it requires.
- A gap summary against the one-day target identifies the largest friction points in
  measurable terms.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2** (onboarding a new data scientist should take less than a day): defines the
  scope of "onboarding" and establishes the measurement baseline the target requires.

# Author and publish the RHOAI enterprise usability whitepaper

## Description

This epic delivers the strategy's documentation requirement (HLR-4): a published
whitepaper describing enterprise usability best practices on RHOAI. The content draws on
the resolved enterprise usability direction (administration configuration practices,
identified integration targets) and the onboarding definition and baseline produced by
the upstream investigations, and is validated for technical accuracy against the RHOAI
architecture context.

When the administration-direction investigation selects an implementation approach for the
administration configuration surface, that selected implementation becomes a blocker of
this epic: it must be added to this epic's dependencies before drafting begins, so the
whitepaper describes the practices that were actually built rather than a plan that
changed after drafting.

## Scope

- Content outline for the whitepaper covering enterprise usability best practices on
  RHOAI across three areas: administration and configuration practices, data scientist
  onboarding practices, and integration with enterprise tooling.
- Draft the whitepaper through the Red Hat docs content process, grounded in the
  investigation decision records (consolidated feedback, selected administration
  direction, named integration targets, onboarding definition and baseline).
- Validate the draft for technical accuracy against the RHOAI architecture context for
  the affected components (Dashboard, Notebooks) and the investigation findings.
- Publish the whitepaper through the designated Red Hat content channel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A content outline exists covering administration, onboarding, and enterprise
  integration practices, and is agreed with the strategy owner.
- The draft is technically reviewed for accuracy against the investigation decision
  records and the RHOAI architecture context (Dashboard and Notebooks component
  documentation); every product claim in the draft traces to a reviewed source.
- The whitepaper is published in the designated Red Hat content channel.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4** (publish a whitepaper describing enterprise usability best practices on
  RHOAI): direct, complete coverage.
